A_open.text: Wednesday afternoon. Intro Biology Lab, third floor. The room smells of bleach and cinnamon.
I scraped the boots. Mostly. The back field comes with you wherever you go.
Safety briefing! Goggles on. No touching. No eating. No dating the lab equipment.
Dating?
Last year a boy proposed to a centrifuge. It said no.
I have the bench. Don't touch anything I haven't named.
Is that a lab rule?
It's my rule. The school's rules are worse.

then.text: You kept my hiding spot. I owe you. Don't make me say that twice.

A_open.text: Hi again! I'm at bench six! I brought snacks for science!
Georgia. No snacks in the lab.
It's a pumpkin muffin. Baking is just chemistry with better lighting.
Confiscated.
The muffins are steaming. They should not still be steaming.
Professor Peters enters, hugging a stack of papers. She sits at the lab computer and glares at it.
Login. LOGIN. I know the password. It's an excellent password.
Professor, try the sticky note.
That is my security feature.
The sticky note on the monitor reads: PASSWORD: ravens123.
Bulletproof.
Today's demonstration. Sample 7. A sealed jar from the old archive.
Decorative gourd extract. Inert. Boring. Twenty minutes, and then you're all free to go.
Then why does the label say DO NOT OPEN?
That's... a joke. From a previous lecturer.
It smells like pumpkin spice.
Everything smells like pumpkin spice in this town.

B_accident.text: Patricia unscrews the lid. A pinch of orange powder goes into a dish of distilled water.
Nothing happens. Several people sigh with relief.
Brad leans in for a better look. A clump of dried mud drops off his boot into the dish.
Oops.
The water hisses. It turns bright orange. Then it begins to glow.
It's supposed to be inert!
Everyone back.
Foam climbs out of the dish, over the bench, and across the floor.
The alarm shrieks. The sprinklers burst on. Glowing foam meets water. There is more foam.
Tradition!
In ten seconds the lab is drowned in glowing orange foam. Four goggled silhouettes stand in it.
Ravens! A raven did this!
Professor, we're on the third floor. The windows are closed.
They're very resourceful.
I'm calling it. Raven.
I think it smells delicious!
Everyone laughs, nervously. Outside, a crow lands a moment too late, and caws in disappointment.
Mr. Bart. You were closest to the dish.

B_accident.prompt: Everyone is looking at Brad. His boots are dripping with foam.

options.text: Confess: it might be my boots

do.text: I think it was my boots. I had mud on them. From the farm.
From which farm?
McVine's. In the back field.
...Gord McVine's.
Thank you for telling me, Mr. Bart. Please don't repeat it.
Your boots did that?!
Nice boots.
Um. I didn't touch anything.
No. Of course not. Raven.
Jane's eyes drop to Brad's boots. They narrow.
Interesting.
Very.

B_accident.text: Cleanup. Everyone. Mr. Bart, as my lab assistant, you will lead.
Walk to someone at their bench and press Action. You have time to help two people.

on_max.text: That's enough for today. Out, all of you. And please, don't discuss this.

stop_p.text: The lights go down. The foam glows softly, like a very large aquarium.
Sample 7 was supposed to be inert. It has been sealed longer than you've been alive.

then.text: You told me about your boots. Few people confess. It was unexpectedly refreshing.

else.text: You look like you're holding something back, Mr. Bart. I won't pry.

then.text: You were not forthcoming about your father, either. I'm making a note.

stop_p.text: This stays between us. If the department hears about it, they'll seal the lab. And everything in it.

stop_p.prompt: Patricia asks Brad for a promise.

do.text: I promise. It's between us.
Thank you. I'm not usually good at trusting people. Or machines.
I can't promise that. Something is wrong here. I think people should know.
That is... honest. I won't ask you to lie. But please, be careful who you tell.

stop_p.text: Good night, Mr. Bart. Mind the foam.

stop_j.text: Jane scoops foam into a jar and screws on the lid.
It's TA tax. I want to compare it to our farm soil.
Sometimes our soil glows too. Dad says it's the moon.

then.text: And it was our soil that set this off. On your boots.

else.text: You didn't say it, but it was your boots, wasn't it?

stop_j.text: The glow is in the back patch. Patch Seven. Dad numbers them. He tells me never to go there.

stop_j.prompt: Brad remembers the orange light from his attic window.

do.text: I saw it. My first night. A glow in the far field. It pulsed.
You saw it? Nobody sees it. Dad says it's my imagination.
Thank you for believing me. I thought I was losing it.
I'm sure it's nothing.
...Sure. Nothing.
Jane doesn't look convinced. She pockets the jar.

stop_s.text: You took photos of the entire accident?
Evidence. Also, it's a good photo.
The tavern has a framed photo behind the bar. The Great Foam Incident. Twenty-five years ago.
My grandfather took it. Nobody talks about it. That's why it's interesting.

do.text: I'd like to see it. Soon.
You've got good instincts. I'll find a time.
Bring an appetite. Our food is worse than the foam.

options.text: Tell her to delete the photos

do.text: Maybe delete those? Before they get Professor Peters in trouble.
No.
But I like that you asked.

stop_g.text: I have foam in my hair! Smell it!
I'd rather not smell your hair.
It smells exactly like pumpkin spice! Like a candle, but from space!

then.text: It smells like your cookie. The one that tingled.
Gord's pumpkins taste like that sometimes. I assumed it was good soil!

stop_g.text: I want to bottle some. For a dessert. A very bold dessert.

stop_g.prompt: Georgia holds up an empty jar, hopefully.

do.text: That foam nearly burned down the lab. Maybe not food.
You're right. I'm not a sensible baker. Thank you for being one.
A tiny swab. Just for sniffing.
You're the best! It'll be an experiment! Totally harmless!
She tucks the swab into a jar and hides it in her bag. Nothing could possibly go wrong.

D_lock.text: Dusk on the quad. The lamps flicker on. Posters on every post: HOMECOMING! BONFIRE! PARADE!
I'm going to ask someone to Homecoming. Calmly. With dignity.
Jane, Sandra, Georgia, and Patricia are each crossing the quad under a different lamp.
Walk up to the person you want to ask. This choice matters.

invite_j.text: Jane! Hi. Homecoming. Are you... going? With... anyone? With me?

then.text: You're asking me?
I'm driving the pumpkin float. I need a co-pilot. And you have the boots.
Yes. I'd like that.

else.text: I'd love to, but Dad has me on float duty. I'm sorry, Brad. Rain check?
Of course! No problem! Rain check!

invite_s.text: Sandra. Homecoming. I thought... maybe... you'd want to go. With me.

then.text: I hate Homecoming.
I hate bonfires. I hate marching bands.
I hate you less than all of them. Yes.

else.text: No. The tavern's busy that night. And I hate marching bands.

invite_g.text: Georgia! Homecoming! I was wondering. Do you want to go with me?

then.text: Wait. You're asking me? Like, on a date?
Yes! Yes! Can I bring muffins? It's a joke! Mostly!

else.text: Oh! I'd love to, but I'm running the cafe booth all day. I'm so sorry!
No, it's fine! Muffins first! Always muffins first!

invite_p.text: Professor Peters. About Homecoming. I thought... would you like to go? With me?

then.text: Mr. Bart. That would be a conflict of interest.
I am a chaperone. I will be at the bonfire. You may walk me there.
It is not a date. It is... a walk. Between colleagues. Of a sort.
A walk. Not a date. Understood.
Good. Eight o'clock. Wear something fireproof.

else.text: Mr. Bart. I am your professor. I'm flattered, and a little mortified.
Please ask someone your own age.
Of course. I'm so sorry. I'll pretend this never happened.
That would be best. By ravens, I imagine.

fallback_ask.text: Brad slumps against a lamppost. Then he hears footsteps behind him.

then.text: Hey. Sorry. I changed my mind. Homecoming. Want to be my float co-pilot?
Wait, what about float duty?
Float duty is a co-pilot. Dad can get over it.
Brad. Don't make this weird.
I hate Homecoming. I hate bonfires. Come with me anyway.
You said the tavern was busy.
I lied. I'm very good at it.
Brad! Wait! I thought about it. I was being silly.
Come with me! I need a taste-tester who tells the truth!
I'd love to.

E_close.text: Later, Brad stands alone under a lamp. Across the quad, the lab windows glow faint orange.
Glowing pumpkins. A professor with a secret. A raven problem.
On a far lamppost the crow sits with something shiny in its beak. A name tag. It doesn't give it back.
